newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fr Telecom should be a public service - Hollande.
newsitem.headline: Fr Telecom should be a public service - Hollande.

text.p: France Telecom must adapt to a competitive environment but this should not jeopardise its mission as a public service, Socialist Francois Hollande said on Thursday.
"We said during the (election) campaign we want a French telecommunications company which remains a public company because it's a public service," Hollande said.

The recently defeated centre-right government planned to sell a minority stake in France Telecom via public share offer scheduled to start this week. The new left-wing government has yet to decide its position since taking power.
"France Telecom is a company which is doing well. It meets user needs and I think it is in the lead technologically," Hollande, who is interim Socialist party secretary, told France Inter radio.
"It fulfils a public service requirement and it also makes a profit. Why would be break something which works? Why carry out reforms which sometimes weaken rather than strengthen companies?" he said.
"But we are in a competitive world, we know that, and the company has to be adapted, without breaking its primary strength, that's to say the very principle of a public service."
